prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Memory from EARLIER parts of the document (do not extract facts from it; use it only to resolve names, aliases and who produces an item):
Greenvale Metro operates a high-frequency urban railway across underground and surface sections with peak, off-peak, and engineering-hour traffic patterns. Communications-Based Train Control system primarily supervises train separation, movement authority, and service regulation on controlled portions. Onboard equipment, wayside control equipment, station interfaces, and central control room interact continuously. Objectives: safe movements, advertised headway, predictable dwell performance, and rapid recovery from routine disturbances. Control room handles strategic regulation; safety-related train and wayside functions handle tactical protection.
Actors: Line Traffic Controller monitors service performance, authorizes planned operational changes, coordinates incident response, and directs recovery when automatic regulation is insufficient. Revenue Train Operator retains responsibility for train readiness, cab procedures, passenger-facing actions, and compliance with instructions through approved operational channels. Field staff participate in fallback voice coordination.
Metro Operations Control System (alias: Lantern) provides control room consolidated train positions, service regulation functions, alarms, and operator command interfaces.
North District Zone Controller and South District Zone Controller calculate safe movement authority limits from train location reports, track occupancy data, and controlled field equipment state.
East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking maintain vital points/signals control at principal junctions; accept only commands satisfying configured safety rules.
Atlas Onboard Controller supervises automatic train protection on each equipped train; uses Dual Channel Odometer data for validated train position/speed estimates.
Train Radio Modem connects each train to Wayside Radio Access Network, the alignment’s train-to-wayside control radio bearer.
Safety Data Communication Network carries safety-related messages between approved control components; engineered for deterministic performance, segregation, and monitored availability.
Service Timetable Server supplies planned service data to central regulation functions. Passenger Information Gateway distributes approved service messages to customer information systems.
Voice Dispatch Console provides fallback voice coordination for Line Traffic Controller, Revenue Train Operator, and field staff when procedural confirmation is required.

Document units:
S017: Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges platform interface indications with the train control environment so that train movement and door operation remain coordinated at fitted stations.
S018: During normal operation, automatic supervision is expected to regulate headways, enforce safe separation, and present the Line Traffic Controller with exceptions rather than routine control steps.
S019: During degraded operation, the system is operated to a defined safe state, with reduced automation, additional human confirmation, and conservative movement arrangements applied according to the operating rulebook.
S020: Loss of train location confidence, loss of communications, or disagreement between vital functions results in protective restriction of movement until the condition is resolved or an approved degraded procedure is invoked.
S021: Signal Maintenance Engineer is assigned the alias Maple for maintenance shorthand in this document.
S022: Signal Maintenance Engineer uses Maintenance Diagnostic Server to review equipment health, correlate alarms, and support restoration without bypassing required operational authority.
S023: Cyber Security Officer oversees access controls, key-management processes supported by Cryptographic Key Management Appliance, and the response to security events that could affect train control availability or integrity.
S024: Metro Operations Control System sends the Crew Login Token Bundle as part of the controlled start-of-duty process.
S025: After successful operator authentication, Atlas Onboard Controller assumes the active train control role when the train is energized and train integrity indications are valid.
S026: The Atlas Onboard Controller is referred to in some installation drawings as Kestrel, but this document uses Atlas Onboard Controller as the canonical name.
S027: Atlas Onboard Controller supervises movement authority processing, onboard speed enforcement, door enable logic, and train interface commands required for CBTC operation.
S028: The controller maintains a safety-critical state machine that separates initialization, protected manual operation, automatic train operation, fallback operation, and cutout conditions.
S029: Movement authority data received from North District Zone Controller and South District Zone Controller is checked for sequence, applicability, and consistency before it is applied onboard.
S030: Interlocking indications associated with East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking are treated as wayside state inputs conveyed through established safety channels.
S031: Dual Channel Odometer provides independent speed and distance measurements derived from axle rotation, inertial sensing, and configured calibration parameters.
S032: Atlas Onboard Controller compares the two odometry channels continuously and degrades the operating mode when the measured divergence exceeds the permitted threshold.
